:::{#exm-complete-inner-product-space}
#### Polynomials are not complete

Let $V$ be the [set](sets.qmd#def-set) of [polynomials](algebra.qmd#def-polynomial) on $[0, 1]$,
with the [inner product](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-inner-product) $\iprod{f}{g} = \int_0^1 f(t)\,g(t)\,dt$.
The [partial sums](algebra.qmd#def-partial-sum) $p_n(t) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{t^k}{k!}$ are a [Cauchy sequence](#def-cauchy-sequence) in $V$,
because they [converge](algebra.qmd#def-convergent-sequence) uniformly on $[0, 1]$ to $e^t$.
The only candidate for a [limit](algebra.qmd#def-sequence-limit) is $e^t$, which is not a [polynomial](algebra.qmd#def-polynomial),
so no polynomial $\vy \in V$ satisfies the condition of @def-complete-inner-product-space,
and $V$ is not [complete](#def-complete-inner-product-space).
<!-- no-figure: the example is a convergence argument about one sequence -->

:::
